topic: what the products do, for the answers that explain (step 67)

facts.claim: Adobe defines Brand Visibility as its application for Generative Engine Optimization, built to improve a brand's visibility, accuracy and influence in AI-driven search.
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility is a generative AI-first application for Generative Engine Optimization (also called Answer Engine Optimization), designed to help brands enhance their visibility, accuracy, and influence in AI-driven search environments.

facts.claim: The product reports on brand presence in AI-generated answers, recommends content changes and automates fixes.
facts.quote: It provides insights into brand presence in AI-generated answers, offers prescriptive content recommendations, and automates optimization fixes.

facts.claim: Customers define, organize and maintain the prompts used to measure visibility.
facts.quote: Prompt Management helps you define, organize, and maintain the prompts used to measure your brand’s visibility across AI platforms.

facts.claim: Suggested prompts and topics come from four sources: Semrush, Google Search Console, Synthetic Personas and Citation Attempt.
facts.quote: Powered by recommendations from Semrush, Google Search Console, Synthetic Personas, and Citation Attempt, Prompt Strategy surfaces topics where your brand has an opportunity to improve visibility as well as topics where your brand already performs well.

facts.claim: Prompts can be added by hand or by bulk CSV upload.
facts.quote: Prompts can be added to Adobe Brand Visibility manually or via bulk upload using the provided .csv template.

facts.claim: The free trial is limited to 100 prompts and one domain; Adobe's pages give no prompt limit for paid licenses.
facts.quote: Customers who activate the trial on or after April 1, 2026 can use up to 100 prompts, one domain, and can deploy optimizations across up to 50 URLs for a single opportunity type.

facts.claim: The Brand Presence (Trial) page names six AI engines for the Platform filter: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity.
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility currently supports ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Co-pilot, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.

facts.claim: The Semrush-powered AI Visibility section covers four engines (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini); Perplexity and Copilot are not named there.
facts.quote: AI Visibility currently supports analysis across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Gemini.

facts.claim: The Brand Visibility metric (formerly Visibility Score) is the percentage of tracked prompts where the brand is mentioned.
facts.quote: Brand Visibility measures the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned.

facts.claim: Mentions counts each AI response once if the brand is mentioned.
facts.quote: Calculated using the same methodology as the trial experience - each response is counted once if your brand is mentioned.

facts.claim: Citations counts each AI response once if the customer's website is cited.
facts.quote: Calculated using the same methodology as the trial experience - each response is counted once if your website is cited.

facts.claim: Source Visibility reports how often the customer's website is used as a source in AI answers.
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility now tracks the metric Source Visibility, which reflects how often your website is used as a source in AI answers.

facts.claim: Share of Voice is visibility weighted by search demand and ranking position, not a simple share of mentions.
facts.quote: Share of Voice now reflects your visibility weighted by search demand and ranking position - a more traffic-oriented measure than a simple mention share.

facts.claim: Sentiment is scored per aspect of the brand within each AI response.
facts.quote: Sentiment is evaluated at the aspect level, allowing a single AI-generated response to contain both positive and negative sentiment for different aspects of your brand.

facts.claim: Position (Trial dashboard) is the brand's relative prominence in AI responses, averaged across weeks.
facts.quote: The relative prominence of your brand in AI responses, calculated as an average across all weeks.

facts.claim: Competitors are set up as tracked 'other brands' (brand name and website) in Brands Management and compared within the same market.
facts.quote: Tracking other brands enables Brand Presence to compare your performance against other brands within the same market.

facts.claim: Tracked brands are compared on how often they are mentioned alongside the customer's brand, by region and category.
facts.quote: With other brands to track, you can see how often other brands are mentioned alongside your brand in different regions and categories and compare their visibility to your own.

facts.claim: Market Comparison (AI Visibility) shows where chosen competitor brands earn mentions and citations the customer's brand does not.
facts.quote: It puts your brand side by side with the other brands you choose, then shows exactly where those brands earn mentions and citations that your brand doesn’t.

facts.claim: URL Inspector shows which of the customer's URLs are cited in AI answers and how often.
facts.quote: It combines visibility, agentic traffic, and referral data at the URL level to give you a granular view of which URLs are cited and how often they appear in responses.

facts.claim: URL Inspector also lists external (third-party) URLs cited in answers relevant to the brand.
facts.quote: The trending URLs competing for citations view, highlights external URLs that are currently cited in answers relevant to your brand, measuring who is winning citations in your space.

facts.claim: For a prompt, the Details view shows the full AI answer, brands mentioned, whether the site was cited and the source URLs.
facts.quote: opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.

facts.claim: Agentic Traffic shows how AI crawlers and chatbots interact with the customer's site.
facts.quote: The Agentic Traffic dashboard shows how AI agents (crawlers and chatbots) interact with your site.

facts.claim: Agentic Traffic data comes from CDN logs, so CDN log forwarding must be configured.
facts.quote: The data used by this dashboard is sourced from the CDN logs so you must configure CDN log forwarding in order to display metrics.

facts.claim: Adobe states no PII is processed or stored from the CDN logs.
facts.quote: No Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is processed or stored at any stage of CDN log ingestion or subsequent data handling.

facts.claim: Referral Traffic shows visitors arriving from external platforms, AI citations and referral links.
facts.quote: Referral Traffic shows how visitors arrive at your site from external platforms, AI citations, and referral links.

facts.claim: The 'Referral Traffic from LLM's' metric is human users who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.
facts.quote: The total traffic from human users who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.

facts.claim: Referral Traffic is built from CDN logs by default; paid customers can add Adobe Analytics or GA4 data for the Business Impact tab.
facts.quote: If your organization is on a paid offer, you can connect Adobe Analytics or Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to add data that measures AI-driven discovery and site engagement.

facts.claim: Opportunities are automatically detected insights on where the site and off-site presence can be improved.
facts.quote: Optimization opportunities are automatically detected insights that show where your site and external presence can be improved to increase brand visibility in AI search.

facts.claim: Opportunities cover on-page content fixes, technical adjustments and off-site (third-party) content.
facts.quote: These optimizations include on-page fixes (adding structured content, canonicals, or summaries), technical adjustments (unblocking AI crawlers or resolving errors) and influencing content on third-party authoritative sites.

facts.claim: Data is collected by executing each Prompt Library prompt on a recurring basis across the supported AI platforms.
facts.quote: Each prompt is executed on a recurring basis across supported AI platforms, allowing Adobe Brand Visibility to monitor how your brand appears in AI-generated responses and how that performance changes over time.

facts.claim: Brand Visibility reports on the prompts the customer actively monitors, not on every user conversation.
facts.quote: It provides ongoing visibility measurements for the prompts you actively monitor, enabling you to evaluate performance, identify trends, and understand how AI systems represent your brand over time.

facts.claim: Adobe notes that the exact prompts people ask LLMs are not disclosed by the LLMs; this is the closest statement on Adobe's pages that reporting is not based on real user conversations.
facts.quote: The exact prompts you ask LLMs are not publicly available because they are not disclosed by the LLMs.

facts.claim: Newly added prompts can take up to 24 hours to start contributing to Brand Presence metrics.
facts.quote: Newly added prompts must be processed before they begin contributing to Brand Presence metrics. Depending on the size of your prompt library, this can take up to 24 hours.

facts.claim: On the legacy Customer Configuration page, Adobe says the scheduled Brand Presence data refresh typically runs at the beginning of each week.
facts.quote: Brand Presence data for newly added prompts will appear during the next scheduled data refresh, which typically runs at the beginning of each week.

facts.claim: Each brand can be tracked in multiple markets, each a country or region plus a language and website.
facts.quote: You can configure multiple markets for each brand to monitor how your brand appears across different regions and languages.

facts.claim: What the Brand Presence dashboards show depends on the Brand Visibility edition.
facts.quote: The Brand Presence experience varies based on your Adobe Brand Visibility edition.

facts.claim: Adobe's own definition of Brand Concierge: an agentic platform for conversational experiences on a brand's websites, mobile apps and other digital properties.
facts.quote: Brand Concierge is an agentic platform that enables businesses and brands to launch personalized conversational experiences on their customer-facing surfaces: websites, mobile apps, and other digital properties.

facts.claim: Adobe says Brand Concierge draws on approved brand content, product catalogs and other trusted sources.
facts.quote: It draws on approved brand content, product catalogs, and other trusted sources, ensuring that all information is brand-safe and up-to-date.

facts.claim: The Site Advisory skill, active by default, is the one that answers general questions such as FAQs, policies and pricing.
facts.quote: Answers general brand questions, including FAQs, policies, pricing, how-to guidance, and support topics

facts.claim: A knowledge source is the content a concierge answers from, and each concierge needs at least one.
facts.quote: A knowledge source is the content that a concierge can use when answering visitor questions. Every concierge requires at least one configured knowledge source.

facts.claim: With a Website Links knowledge source the brand chooses what is crawled: a sitemap, individual URLs, or a CSV list of URLs.
facts.quote: Crawls a sitemap, selected individual URLs, or URLs supplied in a CSV file.

facts.claim: An AEM Sites knowledge source (Content AI index) passes updated AEM Sites content to Brand Concierge without a separate crawl or refresh.
facts.quote: This native integration makes updated AEM Sites content available to Brand Concierge automatically. A separate crawl or refresh step is not required.

facts.claim: A Website Links knowledge source can be refreshed on a schedule, for example weekly, to stay current.
facts.quote: Schedule a refresh frequency, such as weekly on a specified day and time, to keep the knowledge source current as the website changes.

facts.claim: The February 2026 release notes say Brand Concierge supports PDF and DOCX file upload for knowledge sources.
facts.quote: In addition, Brand Concierge now supports PDF/DOCX file upload.

facts.claim: Adobe's go-live guide names three types of knowledge sources: website URLs, PDFs and product spreadsheets.
facts.quote: The three types of knowledge sources: website URLs, PDFs, and product spreadsheets

facts.claim: The concierge answers only from its configured knowledge sources, not from general world knowledge.
facts.quote: A concierge answers questions using only its configured knowledge sources. It does not answer from general world knowledge.

facts.claim: When a question falls outside the knowledge sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information.
facts.quote: If a visitor asks about information outside the configured knowledge sources, the concierge is designed to indicate that it does not have the information instead of generating an unsupported answer.

facts.claim: The brand configures the fallback when the concierge cannot answer: a decline message, alternative questions, self-service links, or escalation to a person.
facts.quote: Options include displaying a graceful “I can’t help with that” message, suggesting alternative questions, linking to self-service resources, or automatically escalating the inquiry to a human agent.

facts.claim: Adobe states every conversation is grounded in the brand's own content and guardrails.
facts.quote: Every conversation is grounded in the brand’s own content and guardrails, and integrations let insights from those conversations flow into the rest of the brand’s ecosystem, such as Marketo Engage.

facts.claim: A Citations chat component controls whether and how source references are shown in a response.
facts.quote: Whether and how source references appear in a response

facts.claim: Guardrails can exclude legal topics, compliance topics or competitor discussions, and the brand reviews and edits them.
facts.quote: For example, guardrails can exclude legal topics, compliance topics, or competitor discussions, while suggestions can provide follow-up prompt ideas.

facts.claim: System-level safety guardrails and content filters always apply, and brand or industry rules are layered on top through instructions.
facts.quote: Safety guardrails, along with content and profanity filters, are enforced at the system level regardless of your own configuration. Anything specific to your brand or industry can be layered on top through the instructions you configure.

facts.claim: Adobe's go-live checklist has the brand review and approve the instructions and guardrails before launch.
facts.quote: Review the concierge instructions and guardrails against applicable brand guidelines.

facts.claim: The brand is responsible for adding a conversational AI disclosure in the conversation experience.
facts.quote: To provide a transparent and trustworthy experience, Adobe Brand Concierge users are responsible for adding a short disclosure within their conversation experience.

facts.claim: Brand voice is configured in the UI through tone, language and personality settings.
facts.quote: You can control your brand voice directly in the UI by configuring elements such as tone (ranging from formal to casual), language (from simple to technical), and personality (for example, helpful, enthusiastic, or professional).

facts.claim: Brand expression is set with attributes such as formality, warmth, playfulness and energy.
facts.quote: Brand expression is set using attributes such as formality, warmth, playfulness, and energy, rather than a single named style.

facts.claim: Evaluations are Adobe's repeatable way to check answer accuracy before wider review.
facts.quote: Evaluations help you build confidence that a concierge’s responses are accurate before the concierge is reviewed by anyone outside your immediate team.

facts.claim: Adobe's go-live guide defines the golden set as real visitor questions paired with ideal answers.
facts.quote: What a golden set is: real visitor questions paired with ideal answers

facts.claim: An out-of-scope evaluation type tests how the concierge handles questions it should not answer.
facts.quote: Checks how the concierge handles questions it should not answer but that are not harmful, such as questions about a competitor or an unrelated topic.

facts.claim: Adobe's checklist calls for a recurring review of transcripts and new evaluation questions after launch.
facts.quote: Establish a recurring process for reviewing conversation transcripts and adding new evaluation questions as they surface.

facts.claim: Handoff to a person is by live chat or meeting booking, with the conversation context carried over.
facts.quote: Live chat and meeting booking are the two ways Brand Concierge hands that conversation to a human without losing the context the visitor already provided.

facts.claim: Live chat and meeting booking are powered by a separate companion product, Adobe Marketo Qualifier, through the Handoff to sales skill.
facts.quote: These capabilities are powered by a companion product called Adobe Marketo Qualifier, and are offered to visitors through the Handoff to sales skill.

facts.claim: Adobe Marketo Qualifier is the product formerly named Sales Qualifier, and it is where representatives take chats and set availability.
facts.quote: both route through Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), where your representatives connect their calendars, set their availability, and take chats.

facts.claim: Adobe's FAQ says the current scope is anonymous visitors, with no live lookup of identity in Real-Time CDP.
facts.quote: In the current scope, Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge base (website and catalog), not from a live lookup of identity or journey state in Real-Time CDP.

facts.claim: The April 2026 release notes label the Real-Time CDP integration Limited Availability.
facts.quote: Brand Concierge Integration with Real-Time CDP (Limited Availability)

facts.claim: What the Limited Availability Real-Time CDP integration does: brings user attributes, behavioral signals and prior interactions into responses.
facts.quote: Enhance the quality and relevance of conversational responses by incorporating Real-Time CDP context, such as user attributes, behavioral signals, and prior interactions to better align replies with user intent.

facts.claim: Adobe's FAQ lists financial services among the industries that can use Brand Concierge.
facts.quote: Brand Concierge can be used across a wide range of industries, including retail and e-commerce, travel and hospitality, financial services, healthcare (with compliance controls), media and entertainment, and technology and software.

facts.claim: Adobe's financial services blueprint says guardrails must keep the agent short of investment advice and define prohibited topics, with compliance and legal review.
facts.quote: the agent must guide customers toward suitable products based on stated needs without constituting investment advice, and prohibited topics (specific return projections, guarantees, comparative performance claims) must be explicitly defined and enforced.

facts.claim: Adobe's financial services blueprint says the content the agent answers from must be compliance-approved descriptions, disclosures and FAQs.
facts.quote: The content integration layer must be grounded in compliance-approved product descriptions, disclosures, and FAQs rather than dynamically generated claims, ensuring every response the agent delivers has been reviewed by legal and regulatory teams before deployment.

facts.claim: Adobe's financial services blueprint requires live agent handoff when a customer's needs exceed the guide's scope.
facts.quote: Live agent handoff must be configured for scenarios in which customer needs exceed the scope of the conversational guide

facts.claim: The sample privacy notice in Adobe's developer guide asks visitors not to enter sensitive personal information such as financial data.
facts.quote: Please do not enter any sensitive personal information (e.g., financial or health data).

facts.claim: The first phase of Adobe's documented migration journey is the Readiness Phase, which checks whether an existing AEM deployment is ready to move.
facts.quote: Begin by determining if your deployment is ready to be moved to AEM as a Cloud Service with the Readiness Phase

facts.claim: The second phase is the Implementation Phase, where code and content are made cloud ready.
facts.quote: Next, make your code and content cloud ready with the Implementation Phase

facts.claim: The third phase is the Go-Live Phase, where the migration is performed (a Post Go-live Phase follows).
facts.quote: After everything is in place, you can perform the migration with the Go-Live Phase

facts.claim: Cloud Acceleration Manager is Adobe's application that guides the move to AEM as a Cloud Service from planning to go-live.
facts.quote: Cloud Acceleration Manager is a cloud-based application designed to guide your IT teams throughout the transition journey starting from planning to going live on Cloud Service.

facts.claim: The Best Practices Analyzer runs against an existing AEM deployment and reports what must be refactored before moving to AEM as a Cloud Service.
facts.quote: This tool generates a report that identifies areas of potential refactoring, which is the first step in the transition journey to AEM as a Cloud Service.

facts.claim: Cloud Manager is the only way to deploy code to AEM as a Cloud Service.
facts.quote: Before you start, you must familiarize yourself with Cloud Manager since it is the sole mechanism for deploying code to AEM as a Cloud Service.

facts.claim: The Content Transfer Tool moves content from an existing AEM instance (on-premise or Adobe Managed Services) to an AEM as a Cloud Service instance; its source is AEM.
facts.quote: The Content Transfer Tool is a tool developed by Adobe that can be used to initiate the migration of existing content from a source AEM instance (on-premise or AMS) to the target AEM Cloud Service instance.

facts.claim: The Content Transfer Tool supports differential (top-up) transfers of only the changes since the last transfer.
facts.quote: The Content Transfer Tool has a feature that supports differential content top-up where it is possible to transfer only changes made since the previous content transfer activity.

facts.claim: The Content Transfer Tool runs on a source AEM instance at version 6.3 or higher, so it does not apply to a non-AEM CMS.
facts.quote: Content Transfer Tool can be run on AEM 6.3 or higher versions only.

facts.claim: Of the three content migration methods Adobe lists for AEM as a Cloud Service (Content Transfer Tool and Package Manager, both from AEM, and Bulk Import), the only one not sourced from AEM is the Bulk Import Service, and it brings in assets from S3 or Azure storage, not pages.
facts.quote: Out of the box Bulk Import Service for Assets (S3/Azure → AEMaaCS)

facts.claim: Adobe's go-live checklist starts with a full production pipeline run including functional and UI testing.
facts.quote: Run an end-to-end production pipeline with functional and UI testing to ensure an always current AEM product experience.

facts.claim: Adobe recommends rehearsing the DNS cutover on a test subdomain with UAT before go-live.
facts.quote: Ensure that the DNS cutover does not introduce unexpected problems. Create a test subdomain to connect your production instance to before you go-live and do a round of UAT testing.

facts.claim: Performance and security tests are run in the stage environment, which is sized like production.
facts.quote: Perform tests in a stage environment. It has the same sizing as production.

facts.claim: A content freeze is planned for the final content top-up before go-live (this applies when content is migrated from AEM with the Content Transfer Tool).
facts.quote: Also, you need to plan for a content freeze when the final content top-up is scheduled.

facts.claim: Cloud Manager runs a code quality gate after the build step in every pipeline.
facts.quote: Code quality testing evaluates your application code based on a set of quality rules. It is the primary purpose of a code-quality only pipeline and is executed immediately following the build step in all production and non-production pipelines.

facts.claim: The Universal Editor is part of AEM Sites and gives authors WYSIWYG editing.
facts.quote: The Universal Editor is a versatile visual editor that is part of Adobe Experience Manager Sites. It enables authors to perform what-you-see-is-what-you-get (WYSIWYG) editing of any headless or headful experience.

facts.claim: Authors create pages from templates that set the page structure, initial content and allowed components.
facts.quote: When an author creates a page, they must select a template, which is used as the basis for the new page. The template defines the structure of the resultant page, any initial content, and the components that can be used when editing the page in the Page Editor.

facts.claim: Core Components are Adobe's standard set of page components for AEM Sites.
facts.quote: The Core Components are a set of standardized Web Content Management (WCM) components for AEM to speed up development time and reduce maintenance cost of your websites.

facts.claim: Adobe's migration guidance starts with a planned review of the existing installation.
facts.quote: it is time to start planning for a review of your existing installation

facts.claim: Adobe says to name a team with roles and responsibilities for the move.
facts.quote: you should identify resources, create a team, and map out roles and responsibilities for the transition process

facts.claim: Adobe recommends agreeing measures of success (KPIs) for the implementation.
facts.quote: it is recommended to establish KPIs for your AEM implementation to help your team focus on what matters the most

facts.claim: For an existing AEM installation the first step is a readiness assessment that shows what needs refactoring.
facts.quote: The first step is to assess your readiness to move from your existing AEM version to Cloud Service and determine areas that require refactoring to be compatible with AEM as a Cloud Service

facts.claim: The AEM Importer works from the rendered pages of an existing website, so it does not depend on which CMS the source site runs.
facts.quote: You start from an existing web page (the DOM is the input).

facts.claim: The AEM Importer outputs docx files (document-based authoring), a content package (AEM authoring with the Universal Editor) or HTML (Document Authoring), all for Edge Delivery Services projects.
facts.quote: The importer creates a docx document, a content package, or HTML for you.

facts.claim: Imported content can be loaded into AEM as a Cloud Service author as a JCR package, for sites authored in the Universal Editor and delivered by Edge Delivery Services.
facts.quote: Using AEM’s package manager or the AEM Import Helper tool to import the JCR package to start your site with AEM authoring and the Universal Editor.

facts.claim: Adobe states Edge Delivery Services supports content migration from non-AEM platforms such as WordPress and Contentful.
facts.quote: Yes, Edge Delivery Services supports content migration from various platforms, including WordPress, Unsplash, Contentful, other AEM instances, and more.

facts.claim: The Experience Modernization Agent migrates sites from other CMS platforms, and its target is Edge Delivery Services.
facts.quote: Supports migrations from a wide range of CMS platforms, legacy AEM, or design systems (like Figma) into production-capable Edge Delivery Services projects

facts.claim: The Experience Modernization Agent cannot migrate into a traditional AEM Sites publish (HTL) implementation. Note: this quote runs from a list heading into its first list item.
facts.quote: The agent does not support the following targets. AEM publish environments where sites use HTL-based delivery

facts.claim: In Adobe's engineer-led (AOE) delivery of the agent, any CMS can be the source as long as the content is publicly reachable static HTML; the page states all such migrations target Edge Delivery Services.
facts.quote: Any CMS platform such as WordPress, Drupal, Sitecore, legacy AEM, SharePoint, or custom solutions can serve as a source. Source content must be publicly accessible over the internet as static HTML.

facts.claim: For Edge Delivery Services, the go-live checklist calls for redirects for retired legacy URLs.
facts.quote: In most migrations there are legacy URLs that are retired. Make sure those are reflected in your redirects spreadsheet

facts.claim: Adobe states Marketo forms can be embedded in Edge Delivery Services pages.
facts.quote: Yes, Marketo forms can be embedded in Edge Delivery Services pages using the Marketo Forms API or iframe embed codes

facts.claim: Adobe defines Edge Delivery Services as a content delivery framework, part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability.
facts.quote: Edge Delivery Services is a modern content delivery framework that re-imagines how websites are built and delivered, optimizing for speed, simplicity, and scalability. It is a core part of Adobe Experience Manager and enables faster digital experiences by pushing rendering and delivery closer to the user, at the edge of the network.

facts.claim: Edge Delivery Services works with the client's own CDN or the Adobe-managed CDN that is included.
facts.quote: It is not a replacement for a content delivery network (CDN), but it integrates seamlessly with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.

facts.claim: Code is managed and deployed from a GitHub repository, and new content needs no rebuild.
facts.quote: Edge Delivery Services uses GitHub so you can manage and deploy code directly from your GitHub repository. New content is added instantly without a rebuild process.

facts.claim: Adobe's go-live checklist sets a Lighthouse score of 100 on mobile and desktop as what a project should produce.
facts.quote: Every AEM project should produce a lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop from Google Pagespeed insights on its respective .aem.live site.

facts.claim: Adobe's advice is to test continuously to keep the Lighthouse score at 100.
facts.quote: It turns out that it is hard to improve your Lighthouse score once it is low, but it is not hard to keep it at 100 if you continuously test.

facts.claim: The content sources Edge Delivery Services takes content from: AEM Authoring (Document Authoring and AEM Sites Author), Microsoft SharePoint and Google Drive.
facts.quote: The bottom tier is where content can be ingested from: AEM Authoring, which includes Document Authoring (DA) as well as AEM Sites Author, Microsoft SharePoint (Word and Excel), or Google Drive (Docs and Sheets).

facts.claim: Authors preview a change at its own URL and share it for review before publishing.
facts.quote: Authors get an instant URL to preview their content changes and share with others for review.

facts.claim: Adobe's importer automates importing and converting many pages of an existing site.
facts.quote: The importer offers the tooling to automate the process for multiple pages of a site to be imported and converted.

facts.claim: Adobe recommends example imports of each page type so authors can confirm the content structure.
facts.quote: It is good practice to make example imports of each page type you wish to import. You can thereby confirm that the authors find the resulting structures intuitive.

facts.claim: A Marketo Engage form has embed code for hosting it on a company's own website.
facts.quote: Access a form’s embed code to host it on your own website.

facts.claim: Prerequisite: the Marketo form must be approved before its embed code is available.
facts.quote: The form must be approved for the embed code to be available.

facts.claim: Limit: Marketo form prefill does not work for a form embedded with the embed code.
facts.quote: Form Prefill does not work when using the form embed code on your own pages or a Marketo landing page.

facts.claim: Marketo Forms 2.0 forms can be embedded on any page of the company's website, not only on Marketo landing pages.
facts.quote: Forms 2.0 lets marketers create web forms without programming knowledge. Forms can reside on Marketo landing pages or be embedded on any page of your website.

facts.claim: Filling out a Marketo form is one of the listed events that ties a visitor's tracked web activity to a known lead in Marketo (the other listed events are arriving from a tracked Marketo email link and a REST Associate Lead call).
facts.quote: When one of these events occurs, Marketo associates the cookie and all related web activity with the known lead.

facts.claim: Adobe describes Marketo Engage as a marketing automation platform that lets you attract, segment and nurture customers.
facts.quote: Adobe Marketo Engage is the world's largest marketing automation platform and a singular solution that lets you attract, segment, and nurture customers.

facts.claim: Each marketing initiative in Marketo Engage is a program.
facts.quote: Programs represent a single marketing initiative.

facts.claim: A Smart Campaign's Smart List defines who is targeted, with filters and triggers.
facts.quote: The Smart List is how you define who you want to target with your Smart Campaign. It has filters and triggers.

facts.claim: A Smart Campaign's flow holds the steps it performs, including wait steps and split choices.
facts.quote: The flow includes the steps you want the Smart Campaign to perform, including Wait steps and split choices.

facts.claim: Adobe's implementation plan includes configuring admin settings, CNAMEs and the Munchkin code.
facts.quote: Configuring admin settings including CNAMEs and Munchkin Code.

facts.claim: Adobe's implementation plan includes testing the automation workflows and the data sync.
facts.quote: Testing automation workflows and data sync

facts.claim: Munchkin, Marketo's JavaScript tracking code, tracks website visitors so automated campaigns can react to their visits.
facts.quote: Marketo's custom JavaScript tracking code, called Munchkin, tracks all individuals who visit your website so you can react to their visits with automated marketing campaigns.

facts.claim: The Salesforce sync is bidirectional for leads, contacts and Salesforce campaigns only; everything else syncs from Salesforce to Marketo.
facts.quote: The sync between Salesforce and Marketo is bidirectional only for leads, contacts, and Salesforce campaigns. In these cases, whenever you make changes in either Salesforce or Marketo, your updates will be reflected in both systems. All other syncs are from Salesforce to Marketo only.

facts.claim: The Email Performance report covers delivered, bounced, opened, clicked and unsubscribed.
facts.quote: Review interactions with your emails: delivered or bounced, opened, clicked, unsubscribed, etc.

facts.claim: The Landing Page Performance report covers visits, conversions and other metrics.
facts.quote: View visits, conversions, and other metrics for your landing pages.

facts.claim: An AEM Forms adaptive form can send captured data to Marketo Engage for smart campaigns and email automation.
facts.quote: Integrating AEM Forms with Adobe Marketo Engage enables users to leverage the capabilities of Marketo Engage to create business logic from captured data and automate workflows, including smart campaigns and email automation. The configured form can send captured data to Marketo Engage for processing.

facts.claim: Prerequisite listed by Adobe for connecting Marketo Engage with AEM Forms: a valid Marketo Engage license.
facts.quote: A valid Adobe Marketo Engage license

facts.claim: Limit: the AEM Forms integration works with Marketo's People (Leads) database only.
facts.quote: AEM only supports the People(Leads) database among the various Marketo databases.

facts.claim: The Submit to Marketo Engage submit action sends adaptive form data to Marketo Engage.
facts.quote: Adaptive Forms editor provides the Submit to Marketo Engage submit action to send Adaptive Forms data to Adobe Marketo Engage for processing.

facts.claim: AEM Forms adds data source connections, e-signatures through Adobe Sign and a Document of Record PDF of the submitted form.
